articles.title: Against the Cartesian Myth of Work/Life Balance: André Gregory’s Extraordinary Letter to Richard Avedon about the Nature of Creativity
articles.highlight: 我们正因自造的笛卡尔裂痕而流血：生活与工作之间那条有害的分界线。
articles.summary: 文章以安德烈·格雷戈里写给理查德·阿维顿的一封信为引，讨论创造力的本质，并批评工作与生活被割裂的现代观念。它把“工作/生活平衡”追溯到工业劳动模式与笛卡尔身心二分，认为这种问题框架要求人分块地活着。值得读的是，它提醒我们重新审视工作狂、效率与创造力之间的关系，而不是把人生切成互不相干的部分。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键 takeaway：真正需要质疑的不是如何分配工作与生活的时间，而是“工作/生活平衡”这一二分框架本身如何塑造我们对创造力与人生的理解。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Half a millennium into our recovery from the civilizational wound Descartes inflicted by severing the body and the mind, we are bleeding with a Cartesian cleft of our own making — the damaging divide between life and work. The notion of a “workaholic,” often worn as a badge on the lapel of the modern ego, presupposes someone who makes work the central axis of life at the expense of living. The very question of “work/life balance,” inherited from the industrial model of labor, asks us to live in parts — a portion of the person doing the working, another doing… read article

en.highlight: we are bleeding with a Cartesian cleft of our own making — the damaging divide between life and work.
en.summary: The piece centers on André Gregory’s letter to Richard Avedon about the nature of creativity and challenges the modern split between work and life. It traces “work/life balance” to the industrial model of labor and the Cartesian divide between body and mind, arguing that this framing asks people to live in parts. It is worth reading as a prompt to reconsider how workaholism, efficiency, and creativity shape a whole life.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway is to question not only how to allocate time between work and life, but the work/life binary itself and how it shapes our understanding of creativity and living.
en.title: Against the Cartesian Myth of Work/Life Balance: André Gregory on the Nature of Creativity

articles.title: Player-YN/BrowserKitten
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + Community signal
articles.summary: 这是一个 GitHub 上的 AI 应用项目，把浏览器智能体的交互反过来做：不是让 AI 自己乱点页面，而是由用户在真实网页上先框选内容，再用自然语言描述想要的结果，最终交付一份可编辑的办公文件。它采用 BYOK（自带密钥）、沙盒执行、无服务端的架构，2844 颗星说明这种“选中即产出”的思路已有不少人关注，值得用来观察浏览器智能体如何从演示走向日常办公交付物。
articles.failureAnalysis: 需求侧存疑：抓网页内容再生成文档，用户可能直接用复制粘贴加通用大模型解决，付费意愿不一定成立；BYOK 把模型调用成本转嫁给用户，既抬高了上手门槛，也让产品体验取决于用户自己配的模型质量。工程与合规约束同样明显：沙盒加无服务器意味着能力被限制在浏览器内，复杂跨系统任务做不了，而读取页面内容、Chrome 商店权限审核与网站反爬都可能成为分发障碍。最大的风险来自平台方：Chrome 内置 Gemini、Edge Copilot 这类原生能力一旦覆盖同类场景，独立插件的生存空间会被迅速压缩。

en.highlight: A selection-first web agent for Chrome: select on the live page, describe the outcome, and take away an editable office file — BYOK, sandboxed, no server.
en.summary: This GitHub AI project inverts the browser-agent interaction: instead of letting the model click around, the user selects content on a real page, describes the desired result, and receives an editable office file. Built with BYOK, a sandbox, and no server, its 2,844 stars suggest real interest in this select-and-deliver pattern.
en.failureAnalysis: Demand is unproven since copy-paste plus a general model may suffice, and BYOK shifts model cost and setup burden onto users; sandboxed, serverless execution also caps task complexity, while Chrome-native AI features could crowd out standalone extensions.
